issues.description: Class PersonService: the template repository declares a constructor that accepts a PersonRepository parameter (constructor injection) whereas the solution repository declares a no-argument constructor that assigns the final personRepository field to null. Template: public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) — intended for constructor injection. Solution: public PersonService() { this.personRepository = null; }. This mismatch changes the dependency-injection approach and will confuse students: they expect to wire PersonRepository via constructor (as shown in the template and typical Spring practice), but the solution's no-arg constructor leaves the repository null and contradicts the intended design (and would cause runtime errors when personRepository is used).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor approach consistent between template and solution. Prefer restoring the constructor that accepts PersonRepository in the solution: public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) { this.personRepository = personRepository; } so both template and solution use constructor injection. Alternatively, if a different injection style is intentional, update the template and problem statement to document and use that same approach. Ensure the final personRepository field is properly initialized by Spring (via constructor injection) in both repositories.
